care.sunlight: Likes light, and resistant to half shade, short period of dormancy in summer, use half shade for better care
care.watering: Water thoroughly 2 times during summer dormancy, keep soil moist in other time, water thoroughly when soil is dry
care.fertilization: Dilute fertilizers following instructions,  apply once monthly in spring and autumn
care.pruning: Remove dead and rotten part timely
care.blooming: Succulent plants, sometimes flowers, white flowers

solutions.advice: Water thoroughly until water drains, then empty the saucer. Avoid letting the root ball stay bone-dry for long.
Hold off watering and improve drainage. Soggy soil risks root rot; check that the pot drains freely.
Move the plant away from cold drafts and windows. Keep within its preferred temperature range.
Reduce heat stress: move out of hot direct sun or away from heaters; increase airflow.
Raise humidity with a tray of pebbles and water, grouping plants, or a humidifier. Avoid soaking fuzzy leaves if applicable.
Increase airflow and avoid misting. Persistent high humidity can encourage fungal spots.
Follow species watering guidance: Water thoroughly 2 times during summer dormancy, keep soil moist in other time, water thoroughly when soil is dry

common_problems: too much direct sun / leaf scorch
keeping soil too wet for a drought-tolerant species
embedding_text: Kalanchoe tomentosa (panda plant, panda bear plant, pussy ears). Soil: Peat and akadama mixed in 3:1 ratio. Sunlight: Likes light, and resistant to half shade, short period of dormancy in summer, use half shade for better care. Watering: Water thoroughly 2 times during summer dormancy, keep soil moist in other time, water thoroughly when soil is dry. Fertilization: Dilute fertilizers following instructions,  apply once monthly in spring and autumn. Pruning: Remove dead and rotten part timely. Ideal temperature 5-35 C. Ideal humidity 15-80%. Ideal soil moisture 7-50. Ideal light 2800-55000 lux. Common problems: overwatering / root rot; underwatering; insufficient light; temperature stress; too much direct sun / leaf scorch; keeping soil too wet for a drought-tolerant species.
